issues.body: The prior-round defect remains unchanged: a_closed_downstream_pipe_is_a_quiet_exit runs Command::new("sh") while using ${PIPESTATUS[0]}, which is Bash-specific, and does not assert out.status.success() or an expected CLI status. A shell substitution failure, or another pipeline failure that never validates the intended CLI path, can therefore satisfy the sole assertion that stderr does not contain "panicked".
issues.fix_hint: Use an explicitly supported Bash pipeline with pipefail and assert successful status, or preferably construct the closed-pipe condition without a shell and assert that the sparq-cli child exits with status 0. Also require stderr to be empty or to match the intended quiet behavior.
issues.title: Broken-pipe test still does not verify a successful CLI exit

verdict.summary: Round 2 does not address the prior major finding. The broken-pipe regression test still invokes a Bash-only PIPESTATUS array through Command::new("sh"), and it still never asserts that the pipeline or CLI exited successfully. On common /bin/sh implementations such as dash, the shell can fail with a bad-substitution error while the test passes because it checks only that stderr lacks "panicked". Consequently the test remains unable to establish the documented quiet-success behavior for a closed downstream pipe.
